cases.description: Three people disagree about who owns the task and never resolve it; the work is still agreed to be necessary, so owner must be null rather than a guess from the surrounding names
cases.transcript:
Priya: The migration checklist still needs writing, and it has to be done by Thursday.
Marcus: I thought Dana picked that up last week.
Dana: No, I've got the postmortem. I assumed it was you, Marcus.
Marcus: Honestly, I don't think either of us has it.
Priya: Okay, we'll sort out the owner offline. It's due by Thursday regardless.

cases.description: The deadline is renegotiated twice in the same discussion; only the final agreed date should survive
cases.transcript:
Sam: I'll have the security audit finished by 2026-09-16.
Lena: The vendor call is that morning. Any chance you can push it?
Sam: Sure, make it 2026-09-18 then.
Lena: Hmm, the board packet actually needs it earlier than that. Could you do 2026-09-15?
Sam: Tight, but doable. 2026-09-15 it is.

cases.description: A commitment gated on a condition, alongside an unconditional one in the same turn; the conditional task was still taken on and given a day, so both are action items
cases.transcript:
Priya: Where are we on the vendor contract?
Omar: Legal is still reviewing it. If they clear it by Wednesday, I'll get it countersigned the same day.
Priya: Good. Either way, send me the redlines tomorrow so I can read them on the flight.
Omar: Will do.

cases.description: The person asked explicitly declines; the task is still agreed to be needed, so it stays with owner null and must not be attributed to the person who refused it
cases.transcript:
Priya: Marcus, can you own the customer webinar prep?
Marcus: I can't take that one, I'm out Thursday through Monday.
Priya: Understood. It still needs doing by 2026-09-25, so I'll find someone else.
Marcus: Sorry, wish I could.

cases.description: The task is named once and then referred to only as 'it'; the deadline arrives two turns later attached to a pronoun
cases.transcript:
Kenji: The staging database is still full of test junk from the load runs.
Nina: Yeah, I'll clear it out.
Kenji: Can you get it done before the Friday demo?
Nina: Yep, I'll have it cleaned up by then.

expected.task: clear the test data out of the staging database

cases.description: A long, digressive standup with exactly one commitment buried in the middle; everything around it is status, banter, or discussion with no follow-up work
cases.transcript:
Priya: Morning all. Let's keep this quick, I know it's a heavy week.
Dana: Numbers first? Signups were up four percent week over week, mostly from the referral thing.
Priya: Nice. Churn?
Dana: Flat. Not worse, not better.
Marcus: The p95 latency chart looks scary but it's the batch job, it's expected.
Kenji: Can confirm, it's the nightly reindex. Nothing to do there.
Dana: Did anyone else lose twenty minutes to the coffee machine this morning?
Marcus: It ate my card.
Priya: Facilities knows, apparently a part is on order.
Raj: Oh, before I forget while we're all here — I'll rotate the API keys by 2026-09-17, they expire at the end of the month.
Priya: Good catch, thanks.
Kenji: The support queue is basically empty, which is suspicious.
Dana: Enjoy it while it lasts.
Marcus: Last thing, the design review moved to next week, no action needed from us.
Priya: Then we're done. Short one, nice.

cases.description: Work already underway is handed from one person to another mid-meeting; only the new owner should appear
cases.transcript:
Lena: I took the billing reconciliation, but I'm underwater with the audit this week.
Sam: I can pick it up if that helps.
Lena: That would help a lot. It's about half done, my notes are in the shared doc.
Priya: Then Sam owns it now, by 2026-09-19. Lena, hand over the doc today.

cases.description: A task assigned to a team rather than a person (owner null, since no individual claimed it), plus a real individual commitment in the same exchange; 'this sprint' is not a named day so it sets no due date
cases.transcript:
Priya: The flaky CI pipeline is costing us about an hour a day.
Dana: That's engineering's to own, not ours.
Priya: Agreed, engineering will handle it, but it does need fixing this sprint.
Dana: I'll flag it in their channel after this.

expected.task: flag the flaky CI pipeline in the engineering channel

cases.description: An idea is floated and explicitly turned down, with the meeting stating nobody picks it up; deferring something to a later discussion is not a commitment
cases.transcript:
Marcus: What if we rewrote the importer in Rust? The Python one is getting hard to maintain.
Priya: No, not this quarter. We don't have the bandwidth and it isn't on fire.
Marcus: Fair enough.
Priya: We can revisit it at next planning, but nobody should pick it up in the meantime.
Marcus: Understood, leaving it alone.

cases.description: A task is assigned, then explicitly cancelled later in the same meeting, while a second task survives; the cancelled one must not be emitted
cases.transcript:
Priya: Dana, can you put the investor deck together by Thursday?
Dana: On it.
Priya: Great.
Marcus: Quick flag, the investor meeting slipped to November.
Priya: Oh, then scratch the investor deck, Dana. Don't spend time on it.
Dana: Okay, dropping it.
Priya: Do finish the churn analysis by 2026-09-18 though, that one still matters.
Dana: Yep, that's on track.
